name: Sunday before Pentecost
description: The waiting for the Holy Spirit between Ascension and Pentecost.
biblicalBasis: The disciples gather in prayer in Jerusalem and wait for the promise (Acts 1:12-14). Jesus had said: "I will not leave you as orphans. I am coming to you" (John 14:18). "The Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things" (John 14:26). "It is for your good that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you" (John 16:7).
significance: The waiting is not passive — the disciples are gathered in prayer and fellowship. Jesus explains that his physical absence is necessary so that the Spirit's universal presence may become possible. The Spirit is not a replacement for Jesus, but his presence in a new form — "another Advocate," who will "lead you into all truth."
liturgicalContext: White or red color. Prayer-focused — gathering in waiting. Some traditions hold a prayer vigil on this Saturday as preparation for Pentecost.
history: The ten days between Ascension and Pentecost were from early church times a special time of prayer. The Pentecost novena (nine days of prayer) has its roots in the disciples' waiting in the upper room. The word "novena" (nine days) comes directly from this.
otConnections: Elijah at Horeb, who waited for the Lord's coming — not in the storm, not in the earthquake, not in the fire, but in the gentle whisper (1 Kings 19:11-13). Israel's waiting in the wilderness between the Exodus and the giving of the Law — fifty days from Passover to Sinai.
